name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,254

clue.text: Career pressure blocks ranked sports player

indicators.note: to block a passage is to sit in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a seed is a player ranked in a tournament draw
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Stress on the job is holding back a top-ranked athlete's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about a working life, but here it is a verb: to career is to rush along wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To career means to move headlong at great velocity, which is what you do when you rush along fast.

clue.text: Finally, gardeners agree on identical plant

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of each word is kept
in a down clue, a piece placed on another sits above it and is written first

blocks.note: the last letter of gardeners
the last letter of agree
identical things are the same

explanation.surface: At last the gardeners settle their argument and choose to grow matching plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' governs both gardeners and agree, so each gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a flowering herb grown for its oily seeds, widely used in cooking.

clue.text: Gospel adherents envisage call to convert

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Devout preachers imagine a summons to bring people over to their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' fits the missionary surface so well that it reads as religious, but it simply signals the rearrangement of envisage call.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical Protestants stress the authority of scripture and spreading the good news, so they are followers of the Gospel.

clue.text: Doctor communication, cancelling mass discipline for horses

indicators.note: to cancel something is to strike it out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor
a message is a communication
M is the physics symbol for mass, taken away

explanation.surface: A doctor's memo calls off group training sessions for the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' sounds like a church service or a crowd, but it is just the physics symbol, and 'cancelling' strikes that one letter out of the communication.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is an equestrian sport in which a horse is trained to perform precise movements, so it is a riding discipline.

clue.text: Famous photographer of giant fish? No thanks

indicators.note: 'no' means without, so the letters that follow are dropped

blocks.note: the manta ray is the giant of the ray family
TA is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone declines a famous snapper's picture of an enormous fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the fanciful idea of a photographer of fish; taking TA from MANTA RAY leaves the name. Ta is casual British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Ray was an American surrealist artist celebrated for his experimental portrait and fashion photography in Paris.

clue.text: Born north of border? It’s a temporary setback

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever is north sits higher and so is written first

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for born in records
a lip is the edge or rim of something

explanation.surface: Being born just across the northern frontier is shrugged off as a minor hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests a national frontier, especially with 'north of', but it is the edge of a cup or wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a brief, minor interruption or dip, quickly recovered from, like a short-lived problem.

clue.text: Permanent livestock accommodation

blocks.note: first meaning: steady and lasting, not likely to change
second meaning: a building where horses are kept

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a lasting barn; split it into an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something fixed and steady and a noun for a building that houses horses.

clue.text: Noble occupying correct part of vehicle?

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: correct means right
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat sitting in the proper seat of a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the answer is one specific component of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp fixed at the back of a car or bicycle is one component of a vehicle.

clue.text: Jason’s prize: great delight about ancient fine church

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: glee is great delight
olden means of long ago
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Jason's reward brings great joy concerning an old, beautiful church.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDEN and F go together inside GLEE, then CE ends the answer. CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Jason and the Argonauts sailed to Colchis to seize the wool of a magical winged ram.

clue.text: Fish slide smoothly on surface

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat sea fish related to rays
second meaning: to glide over ice or a floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a verb in a sentence about angling; it is a noun naming a flat sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat cartilaginous sea creature and the act of gliding over ice on blades.

clue.text: Site in which threads are systematically removed?

definitions.text: Site in which threads are systematically removed?

blocks.clueFragment: Site in which threads are systematically removed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a factory or workshop where strands of yarn are pulled out of fabric
setter's reading: threads is slang for clothes, taken off one by one as a performance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Threads' sounds like textile work, but it is informal slang for clothing, and the place is an entertainment venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where dancers undress piece by piece for an audience is where garments come off in a routine.

clue.text: Animal seen in New England

indicators.note: something seen in a place is visible inside it, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: spans the end of New and the start of England

explanation.surface: Some creature spotted in the north-eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the word break: nEW England.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a farm animal, so the general word covers this specific creature.

clue.text: We say our cast accepts ecstasy — I take that back

indicators.note: to cast metal is to remould it, so the letters are reshaped
to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A theatre company announces its cast has taken drugs, then hurriedly retracts the statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatrical troupe but signals the rearrangement; E for ecstasy then goes into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command restoring the previous position is also used in speech to withdraw a remark just made.

clue.text: Calm UN regulation protecting twin females

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: taken as written
a rule is a regulation
F for female, twice

explanation.surface: A soothing United Nations rule designed to safeguard pairs of twin sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin females' is the standard abbreviation for female, doubled; 'Calm' here is a verb, to soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth ruffled feelings is to soothe or settle someone, so the verb means to quieten them.

clue.text: Sheep lice treated with organic compound

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to rearrange
an ester is an organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol

explanation.surface: A flock's parasites are dealt with using a chemical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' fits the vet's surface, but it signals the rearrangement of lice. Leicester is an English county that gave its name to a breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leicester is a long-wool breed of domestic animal developed in eighteenth-century England, so it is a kind of ovine livestock.

clue.text: Fat eater emptied food store

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, so only its outside letters remain

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
the first and last letters of eater

explanation.surface: A greedy overweight diner has raided and cleared out the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat eater' reads as a description of a person, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard where provisions are kept, essentially a pantry for groceries.

clue.text: Decorative accessory on dresser made of pine — it cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken, so its letters come apart and are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An ornament on a pine chest of drawers has split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' suggests furniture, which the pine supports, but it is a person getting dressed, wearing the accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental clasp holding a necktie in place is jewellery worn by someone smartly clothed.

clue.text: Porky Pig seen naked in Facebook

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters go and the middle stays
something in another sits within it, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: FB is the common abbreviation for Facebook
the middle letter of pig

explanation.surface: The cartoon pig Porky has been posted in the nude on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky Pig' looks like the cartoon character, but the words split apart. Porky is British rhyming slang: porky pie, lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Through rhyming slang a porky is an untruth, and a small untruth is a minor lie told casually.

clue.text: Criminal reportedly vetoed Congress?

indicators.note: reportedly means according to what is said, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: vetoed is banned and congress, as in sex, is it

explanation.surface: A crook is said to have overruled the American legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US parliament; the question mark flags its other sense of sexual intercourse, which crosswords often call it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber or outlaw, typically one of a gang attacking travellers.

clue.text: Part of Sun lunch sometimes prepared before Sat

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been made up from raw materials, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Sunday meal component that is sometimes cooked ahead, on Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared before Sat' sounds like cooking ahead of the weekend; 'prepared' is the signal and 'before Sat' is the fodder. Sun abbreviates Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of oven-cooked meat is the traditional centrepiece of the British Sunday dinner, though not every week.

clue.text: Fool turning up at last, any minute

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upward means the letters read from bottom to top
at last points to the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a nit is a foolish person
the final letter of any

explanation.surface: An idiot who finally shows up could arrive any time now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Any minute' reads as a time phrase, but 'minute' is the adjective meaning very small. Nit is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, is a synonym for extremely small in size.

clue.text: Skilfully handle all competitors

blocks.note: first meaning: to deal deftly with questions or problems
second meaning: everyone taking part in a race or contest

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests managing rivals; split it into a verb and a collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for deftly fielding awkward questions and a noun for the entire set of entrants in a race.

clue.text: Vitally important lease isn’t up for renewal

indicators.note: something up for renewal is about to be remade, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: It matters a great deal that the rental agreement is not due to be renegotiated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for renewal' fits the tenancy surface naturally, which hides its role as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely necessary or indispensable is crucial, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Regular time for what happens

blocks.note: even means regular or steady
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A routine slot set aside for whatever occurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular time' reads as one phrase, but the words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or incident is something that takes place, so the noun means a happening.
